classification.difficultyReason: Select the longest side, compare its square with the other two squared lengths and, when equal, name the angle opposite that side.

content.prompt: Decide whether each of the triangles below is right-angled. If it is, name the right angle.

spec.description: Triangle with A upper right, B lower left and C lower right; no right-angle mark.
spec.answerVisibility: All side lengths and vertex names are supplied; the right-angle decision is withheld.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}10^2+24^2&=100+576\\10^2+24^2&=676\\26^2&=676\end{align*}$$
Since $10^2+24^2=26^2$, the triangle is right-angled by the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem. The right angle is opposite $AB$, so $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle with C upper left, B upper right and A below C; no right-angle mark. The apparent square corner is not evidence of a right angle.
spec.answerVisibility: All side lengths and vertex names are supplied; the right-angle decision is withheld.
